newsitem.title: USA: Vietnam taking steps to boost foreign investment.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam taking steps to boost foreign investment.

text.p: Vietnam is taking steps to reform its daunting legal system and cumbersome administrative bureaucracy in an effort to boost foreign investment, but changes will be gradual, experts said on Monday.

"Overall I think Vietnam is adopting a very practical approach to legal reform," said John Dick, chief representative at Vietnam-based Freehill Hollingdale & Page. "But certainly it will take some years."
Dick was among several panelists speaking at a seminar sponsored by the World Bank Group and International Monetary Fund, and titled "Vietnam: Business Opportunities in the Next Decade of Reform."

During the discussion, Pham Chi Lan, Secretary General of the Vietnam Chamber of Commerce & Industry, admitted that the legal environment in the country "is still incomplete and needs further reform in the coming years."
She said however, that government authorities are aware of the "lack of transparency" on legal issues and are taking concrete measures to improve the system.
Encouraging foreign investment, which has increased rapidly in recent years, is a key element of Vietnam's reform strategy.
It will play a key role in determining whether Vietnam reaches the development targets tied to the country's recently adopted five-year socio-economic strategy.

Cao Sy Kiem, Governor of the State Bank of Vietnam, said the goal is to achieve an average annual economic growth rate of nine to 10 percent, annual growth in industrial output of 14 to 15 percent and single digit inflation over the coming five years.
